::: {.notes}
So I'm here to talk about Portolan, a project we've been working on for nine or so months, and publicly launched last month. But this talk is going to be a bit different from every other Portolan talk you'll see, because this audience is different from our typical target audience.
:::

:::

::: {.notes}
That's because our target audience is really people who have never heard of CNG. One of our main goals with Portolan is to take cloud-native geospatial beyond early adopters and to the mainstream. I believe we're right at the chasm, and our next users don't care about cool technology.
:::


## {#slide-03}

::: {.slide-head}
[Why Portolan]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body}
```{=html}
<div class="cols">
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.2s">
    <h3>Open</h3>
    <p>GeoParquet, PMTiles, COG, STAC. Opens in QGIS, ArcGIS, pandas, BigQuery.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.45s">
    <h3>Cheap and sovereign</h3>
    <p>Files in a bucket. Any provider, any jurisdiction. No servers.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.7s">
    <h3>For people and agents</h3>
    <p>Documented well enough that both can actually use it.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
So most of the talks we give have slides that look like this, articulating the 'why' — and most of that is just trumpeting everything that CNG gets you. So a common reaction from people who are deep in CNG is "why would I need this?"

And if you already know how to tune each format, and you stay up to date with all the latest advances…
:::


## {#slide-04}

::: {.center-v}
[Portolan is for everyone else.]{.statement .a-rise style="--d:0.3s"}
:::

::: {.notes}
…and always make amazing catalogs — then the answer is, you don't. Portolan is for everyone else.

A Portolan catalog is a STAC catalog, with guidance and tools to help new users.
:::


## {#slide-05}

::: {.slide-head}
[A Portolan catalog]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body}
```{=html}
<pre class="tree a-fade" style="--d:0.2s">catalog.json
├── <span class="k">AGENTS.md</span>                     <span class="c">for agents</span>
├── <span class="k">README.md</span>                     <span class="c">for people</span>
└── collections/
    ├── land-use/
    │   ├── collection.json
    │   ├── <span class="k">style.json</span>            <span class="c">cartography, as an asset</span>
    │   ├── land-use.pmtiles
    │   └── <span class="k">admin=*/*.parquet</span>     <span class="c">glob, partition extension</span>
    └── imagery/
        ├── collection.json
        ├── <span class="k">items.parquet</span>         <span class="c">stac-geoparquet</span>
        └── cogs/<span class="k">*.tif</span></pre>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
Structurally it'll look very familiar. But we take out a lot of the choice that CNG gives you, in favour of requirements — like always spatially sort your GeoParquet, with reasonably sized row groups and zstd compression; or provide sufficient overviews for your COGs and write gdal stats, so tile servers render consistently. And we provide a validator to help users and agents get it right.
:::


## {#slide-06 .bleed}

```{=html}
<video class="fill" src="media/data-browser.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
```

::: {.notes}
Our goal is to enable CNG to completely replace the traditional spatial data infrastructure APIs and portals. So we take a holistic lens on the ecosystem, to make sure we have all the pieces to deliver a complete experience — and we encourage custom theming of the tools, to make them feel integrated with the data provider.
:::


## {#slide-07}

::: {.slide-head}
[Making vector work in a browser]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body .split}
```{=html}
<figure class="shot" style="flex:1.35 1 0">
  <div class="placeholder">Placeholder — vector-in-the-browser recording</div>
</figure>
<ul class="ruled a-fade" style="--d:0.3s">
  <li>Styles as STAC assets</li>
  <li>Glob in the partition extension</li>
  <li>The table extension, required</li>
</ul>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
The holistic lens has forced us to solve a lot of issues at the edges of the formats, and it has led to a few advances that are interesting to people in this room: including styles as assets in a STAC catalog, extending the STAC partition extension with glob syntax, and requiring the table extension.
:::


## {#slide-08 .bleed}

```{=html}
<video class="fill" src="media/s2-search.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
```

::: {.notes}
We're embracing stac-geoparquet to enable completely cloud-native search. I just put up all of Sentinel-2 in GeoParquet, and it took a bulk processing job I had from 20 hours down to 16 minutes. And you can see it also powering sub-second search responses across the entire Sentinel-2 archive.
:::


## {#slide-09 .bleed}

```{=html}
<video class="fill" src="media/tulip-chat.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
```

::: {.notes}
And we added an AGENTS.md file, which enables pretty magical direct interaction with geospatial data. Most every agent can install DuckDB and do advanced geospatial analysis, and we believe this will ultimately open up the power of geospatial to many more users.
:::


## {#slide-10 .bleed}

```{=html}
<video class="fill" src="media/catalog-demo.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
```

::: {.notes}
We've also invested in various agentic skills to make it easy to translate entire catalogs into Portolan, and we're continually improving the connectors to ArcGIS, WFS and others. So making a great catalog is incredibly easy.

One prompt: the agent pulls the datasets, converts them, writes the documentation, publishes to Source Cooperative — and there it is in the browser.
:::


## {#slide-11}

::: {.slide-head}
[A complete ecosystem]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body}
```{=html}
<div class="eco">
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.15s"><span class="n">01</span><h3>Spec<br>+ validator</h3></div>
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.35s"><span class="n">02</span><h3>CLI<br>+ skills</h3></div>
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.55s"><span class="n">03</span><h3>Browser</h3></div>
  <div class="a-rise" style="--d:0.75s"><span class="n">04</span><h3>Registry</h3></div>
</div>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
We are aiming for a complete ecosystem, and we've been leveraging all the amazing work that this community has created. We're still targeting early adopters, and our goal is to have every geospatial tool understand Portolan, and to get hundreds of catalogs of open data in the format.
:::


## {#slide-12}

::: {.slide-head}
[Yesterday's sprint]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body .split}
```{=html}
<figure class="shot" style="flex:1.5 1 0">
  <div class="placeholder">Placeholder — photo from yesterday's sprint</div>
</figure>
<div class="stats" style="flex-direction:column; gap:2.4rem">
```

We're aiming to do that by working with as many of you as possible. We had a great sprint yesterday, where twelve of us produced X new catalogs with Y amounts of new data. Our focus for now is really the data — converting all the great global datasets, along with many key regional ones.
:::


## {#slide-13 .bleed}

```{=html}
<video class="fill" src="media/firms-explorer.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
```

::: {.notes}
With each new dataset converted, I hope we push the cloud-native geospatial ecosystem forward in a different way — that it becomes a community of people making great data products and pushing the edges of what's possible with CNG. This was an explorer I made on top of a FIRMS fire data catalog, pushing the bounds of interactivity across twenty years of global data.
:::


## {#slide-14 .bleed}

```{=html}
<video class="fill" src="media/registry.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
```

::: {.notes}
The other key bit of the ecosystem is the Portolan Registry, where all high quality catalogs get registered for everyone to query. It's like STAC Index, but with a guarantee to users that the data will always be well-documented and performant.
:::


## {#slide-15 .bleed}

```{=html}
<video class="fill" src="media/finland-demo.mp4" data-autoplay muted loop playsinline></video>
```

::: {.notes}
The goal is to gather enough global data to be able to answer complex geospatial questions with LLMs. We want to enable the type of analysis that would previously take a team of geospatial experts to pull in all the data and extract insights from. This was an early demo showing how you can answer questions about data centres by pulling data in from five different Portolan catalogs.
:::


## {#slide-16}

::: {.center-v}
[All the world's data, in CNG formats.]{.statement .a-rise style="--d:0.2s"}
:::

::: {.notes}
We want to see all the world's data in CNG formats. We believe AI can help get us there, and that the world's data in CNG formats will enable anyone to use AI to get geospatial insights — increasing the users of geospatial information by at least a couple of orders of magnitude.
:::


## {#slide-17}

::: {.slide-head}
[Then, back across the chasm]{.headline}
:::

::: {.slide-body}
```{=html}
<ol class="ruled big">
  <li class="a-rise" style="--d:0.2s">A hundred catalogs</li>
  <li class="a-rise" style="--d:0.45s">Case studies and logos</li>
  <li class="a-rise" style="--d:0.7s">The early majority</li>
</ol>
```
:::

::: {.notes}
Once we have a hundred or so catalogs and get the tools really nailed, our next goal will be to start to go after the early majority. We aim to get a number of case studies and logos in place to show that it's not just the crazy early adopters — but instead that it would be crazy not to adopt Portolan.
:::
